# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-WEAR-01 (EyePACS, wearing camera, United States)
- Period: week 9 (starting 2026-03-02)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift identified that retinal scans from this clinic no longer conform to the baseline characteristics of the AI validation dataset (observed drift score of 0.96, where 0.5 represents training characteristics and 1 represents a clear deviation). 

Consequently, the catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) cannot be verified from the 50 scans evaluated during this week, and expert reference grades for these scans have not yet been received.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of potentially missed cases cannot be estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
Severe degradation in image sharpness and overall image quality at the clinic, likely resulting from hardware faults or image capture technique issues. (category: camera or image quality; confidence 85%; source: gemini)

Evidence:
- Drift score of 0.96 observed over 50 scans in week 9.
- Mean sharpness decreased from 0.000399 in training to 1.21e-05 in flagged scans, representing a relative change of -0.97.
- Mean image quality dropped from 0.5 in training to 0.208, representing a relative change of -0.584.
- Mean brightness dropped from 0.373 in training to 0.313, representing a relative change of -0.161.
- Evidence strength is moderate to strong: although the sample size is small at 50 scans, the drop in sharpness and quality is extreme and is corroborated by visual inspection showing blurry, dark scans.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift has paused AI deployment at this clinic because the scans have drifted beyond the model's validated baseline, meaning the catch rate cannot be verified. It is recommended that scans from this clinic are referred for human grading until the following checks are completed:

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect and clean the camera lens for smudges, dust, or fingerprints.
- [ ] Verify flash brightness settings and auto-focus functionality on the camera.
- [ ] Retrain operators at clinic US-WEAR-01 on proper image acquisition and patient positioning.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alert forms part of ongoing post-market monitoring of the device in commercial use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model modifications made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: refer to recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
